how-retirement-ends-a-name.text: Run the retirement rows on a real devnet with the packaged runner, using a private shallow temporary directory and the blueprint built from this commit. The diagram shows the lifecycle: an active record retires by controller or quorum into completion-only custody, and anyone completes it permissionlessly, burning the representative while the key stays occupied. Two failure controls ship alongside: one makes a refused row valid, the other matches refusals against an impossible marker. Both must fail after executing rows.

limits-and-next-steps.text: The representative is a real NFT minted under the applied policy and burned exactly once at completion. Custody is spent only by permissionless completion; withdrawal without burn, burn without transition, mismatched pairings, and re-registration after Over all refuse, each with its reason named.

what-the-retirement-run-observes.text: Each accepted route proves custody from the chain: the representative is observed at the custody script and the record is observed gone. The over name additionally recovers first, retires through its recovered controller, and completes with empty required signers and one fresh fee witness. Refusals name their script and purpose, including a stored quorum that duplicates one member to bind the distinctness the model demands. The replay is refused by the ledger itself.

what-the-run-observes.text: The accepted row installs the reveal with a fresh commitment and proves preservation and transfer from the chain. Each refusal is a single-defect mutant refused in phase two naming the application validator. Replay and the old controller are refused against the genuine successor, maintenance under the recovered key succeeds, and the state after refusals is unchanged.

what-you-can-do.text: Run the eleven recovery rows on a real devnet with the packaged runner, using a private shallow temporary directory and the blueprint built from this commit. Two failure controls ship alongside: one makes a refused row valid, the other matches refusals against an impossible marker. Both must fail after executing rows.

who-this-is-for.text: This page is for a holder who lost the everyday control key but committed to a next controller in advance, and for a holder — or the registration quorum — who wants to end a name permanently into completion-only custody. You spend the record with the committed address or the quorum alone, and the chain hands over control or ends the name.
